match_note: v1 (23 Apr 2026) predates the arXiv paper R2 cites (2605.22282), which the authors say appeared a month after their initial submission; v1 has the items referees flag as missing or unclear ('Combining all known techniques', Fig. 4h simulation only, Fig. S4b, >1300 µm² devices) and lacks the revisions (membrane-transfer and CVD references, AFM-cutting detail, narrow-channel imaging, thin-RMG device).

concerns.quote: One could mention that others have also used flexible membranes for 2D-transfer
concerns.summary: Suggests citing prior flexible-membrane and soap-film transfer methods.

concerns.quote: the authors do not detail the low-pressure transfer technique even though they claim it is essential to reach a final device yield of 90%
concerns.summary: The vdW assembly steps behind the ~90% device yield (exclusion of Bernal microdomains, AFM cutting of domains) are not described; R3 notes cutting is not mentioned among 'all known techniques'.

concerns.quote: Has the low-pressure assembly technique been developed by the authors or is this commonly known in the community? If so, are there references to cite?
concerns.summary: Asks whether the low-pressure transfer technique is new or needs citations.

concerns.quote: the authors lack to compare to other exfoliation techniques that claim to increase the RMG yield
concerns.summary: Asks for comparison with another recently reported method for raising RMG yield.

concerns.quote: What is new compared to Bernal stacking for RMG devices in the hydrodynamic regime for example?
concerns.summary: The motivation for the transport-regime results and how RMG differs from Bernal graphite is not explained.

concerns.quote: the main novelty of the manuscript lies in the novel exfoliation and vdw-assembly technique. This is surely worth publishing, however, there remains the question whether Nature Nanotechnology is the appropriate choice.
concerns.summary: Since high-quality transport is established, novelty rests on the fabrication method, questioning fit for the journal.

concerns.quote: Why is the rhombohedral stacking limited to ~30% of the surface? Do the authors envision protocols to further enhance that fraction? What is the limiting mechanism?
concerns.summary: Asks what limits the rhombohedral fraction to about 30%.

concerns.quote: Is it so surprising to find a ballistic transport regime in a 13-layer graphite flake in the high-density regime?
concerns.summary: Questions whether ballistic transport at high density in 13-layer graphite is notable.

concerns.quote: How are the authors sure that the RMG flakes do not contain some polytypes that are not purely rhombohedral stacking
concerns.summary: IR and sMIM contrast may not exclude mixed polytypes; how is pure rhombohedral stacking confirmed?

concerns.quote: Does the AFM cleaning, prior to the deposition of the top gate change the stacking order?
concerns.summary: Asks why the top gate is placed last and whether AFM cleaning alters stacking.

concerns.quote: The authors should extend the statistics of Fig.1g,h also to the thickness of the obtained flakes and RMG domains therein.
concerns.summary: Yield statistics are not broken down by layer number, and layer thickness is not labelled throughout.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: there is no evidence that the thin limit can be explored with this new technique, highlighting a possible key drawback.
concerns.summary: No evidence that thin RMG devices hosting correlated phases can be made with the method.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the paper reports a simulation of the spatial current flow (Fig.4h), but no experimental Biot-Savart imaging.
concerns.summary: The narrow-channel device has only simulated, not imaged, current flow.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Promotion of rhombohedral stacking from mechanical stress was already shown in CVD-grown graphene
concerns.summary: Prior stress-induced rhombohedral stacking in CVD graphene should be cited.

concerns.quote: A device with area >1300 um^2 is claimed: is an optical image of this specific device shown in the paper?
concerns.summary: Asks whether the >1300 µm² device is shown.

concerns.quote: Which graphite crystals are used as starting material? Which tape is employed?
concerns.summary: Starting graphite and tape are not specified, hindering reproduction.

concerns.quote: The "single sequence transfer" mentioned in Fig. S4b (x axis) is not properly defined in the paper or methods.
concerns.summary: An axis label term in Fig. S4b is undefined.

later_concerns.quote: The newly added Ref. 47, concerning membrane transfer techniques, seems to be unrelated.
later_concerns.summary: Round 2: a newly added reference appears irrelevant.
